title: One readable work in the Library
description: Reading structure over a corpus this repository already ships. A work file carries NO statutory text: `corpus` is a pointer into data/rules/text/*.json or data/law/*.json, and `toc`/`readingOrder` name unit ids inside it. Written by scripts/ingest/library_seed.py; the runtime half is src/schemas/library.ts.

corpus.description: A POINTER to the dataset that owns the text. Never a copy of it.

unitLabel.description: What one unit is called here — Rule, Section or Paragraph.

tocSource.description: Where the table of contents came from. `chapters` — the corpus records a chapter per unit. `numbering` — the unit numbers themselves carry the division (CSMOP's `4.7`). `flat` — the corpus holds no division at all, so there is one node per unit and NOTHING was invented (docs/DATA-GAPS.md #70).

readingOrder.description: Every unit id in the pointed-at corpus, in document order.

examTags.description: This project's own navigation labels. Every one must have a bilingual label in src/lib/library/tags.ts, which tests/library-data.test.ts asserts.

verify.description: True wherever any Hindi in this work is authored or curated by this project rather than published. True on every work so far.

practiseCounts.description: unit id -> how many APPROVED Trainer cards cite it, counted at build time from data/rules/cards/*.json. Empty for a law work: no card cites a law section. Counted here so the reader page can offer 'practise this' without downloading up to 1.1 MB of cards to find out whether there is anything to practise.

unitIds.description: Every unit under this node, flattened. A leaf carries exactly one.

excerpt.description: The opening of the unit, capped, present ONLY on a leaf whose heading is missing in one or both languages. Four of the twelve rule books publish no heading this repository could extract (FR/SR, CSMOP and a handful of GFR/CCS rules), so without this an English table of contents over them would be a column of bare numbers. Same fallback scripts/authoring/make_cards.py already uses on a rule card's front. A quotation for navigation, never the provision itself.
